clue.text: Top closers might get them for buttons

definitions.text: Top closers might get them for buttons

parts.words: Top closers might get them for buttons
parts.note: fasteners for the top of a garment that could replace buttons; 'top' reads as best and 'closers' as finishers, but the clue means garment fastenings

explanation.definitionFit: Zip fasteners close tops and can be used on garments in place of buttons.

clue.text: Supplying and using is peculiar

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so these letters are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the act of supplying and the act of using make a strange pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' rearranges the letters of USING and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Issuing something is handing it out, the same as supplying it.

clue.text: He'd sin if wicked!

indicators.note: wicked can mean twisted or bad, so the letters before it are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A moral warning that a man would fall into sin if he were wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' rearranges HEDSINIF, the letters of He'd sin if; the whole clue also describes a devilishly evil person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiendish person is devilishly cruel, the sort who would sin if wicked.

clue.text: Cast female lead in drama

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a female

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of drama

explanation.surface: A casting director picks a woman for the starring role in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests choosing actors for a play, but it is the definition, meaning throw off.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something, like a snake its skin, is to cast it off.

clue.text: Choose to speak for the people who vote

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to speak formally in public

explanation.surface: A candidate is chosen to speak on behalf of the voters.
explanation.definitionFit: An electorate is the whole body of voters in a constituency or country.

clue.text: Gain access, turning up in secret negotiations

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone gets inside, emerging in the middle of confidential talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the hidden letters RETNE inside secret negotiations, and 'turning up' (a down clue) reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a place is to go into it, getting in.

clue.text: makes a comeback — different leader with staying power

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'makes a comeback — different leader with staying power': the opening cross-reference (27, ANIMATE, reversed with its first letter changed) is cut off, and no scan or search gives the full printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: makes a comeback — different leader with staying power

clue.text: Policeman noisily runs ashore to these trees

parts.note: copper is British slang for a police officer

indicators.note: noisily says the word is said out loud and spelt by its sound

parts.note: to beach a boat is to run it ashore, so runs ashore gives beaches

explanation.surface: A police officer runs up the beach towards a stand of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: COPPER is everyday British slang for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper beeches are beech trees with purplish-red leaves.

clue.text: A banking term for reputation and class

parts.note: standing means status or reputation
an order is a rank or class, as in the lower orders

explanation.surface: A glossary entry offers a banking expression meaning good name and social rank.
explanation.walkthrough: A standing order is a British bank instruction to pay a fixed sum regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing order is a regular payment instruction given to a bank, so a term from banking.

clue.text: Lewd display on outside broadcast

indicators.note: in an across clue on puts the display after the broadcast

parts.note: a scene is a public display, as in making a scene

explanation.surface: Something indecent appears on a programme filmed on location.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene material is indecent and offensive, which is what lewd means.

clue.text: A minor actor to court and take out

parts.note: an extra is a minor actor in a crowd scene

explanation.surface: A bit-part player is dragged to court and removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to pull or draw it out.

clue.text: Talking lions will be closely investigated

indicators.note: Talking means the word is spoken, so the letters follow its sound

parts.note: a group of lions is called a pride

explanation.surface: Lions that can speak will be studied in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To have pried is to have looked or inquired nosily and closely.

clue.text: The Virgin autograph hunter might see it!

explanation.surface: A fan seeking a signature spots someone famous called the Virgin.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgo, the Virgin, is a sign of the zodiac; read as two words, a fan sees a celebrity sign an autograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo, symbolised by a virgin, is a zodiac sign; an autograph collector watches a celebrity write a signature.

clue.text: Publicity that has a respectable look when reported

indicators.note: when reported means the phrase is spoken and the letters follow its sound

parts.note: proper means respectable and a gander is British slang for a look, giving a proper gander

explanation.surface: Publicity that gives off an air of decency when it reaches the news.
explanation.walkthrough: Having a GANDER is everyday British slang for taking a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is publicity material spread to promote a cause or view.

clue.text: The official record holders are doctors

explanation.surface: The people keeping official records turn out to be physicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Registrars keep official registers such as births and marriages; in British hospitals a registrar is a grade of doctor below consultant.

clue.text: One is on duty to provide transport

indicators.note: in an across clue is on places the letter after the duty

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone working a shift offers people a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a form of hired transport.

clue.text: Smile on a cook's pudding?

indicators.note: cook is a verb here, to cook the books, so the letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: Should one smile at a cook's milk pudding?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook's' means cook is: it rearranges SMILEON into SEMOLIN, and the clue's A is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is a milk pudding made from coarse wheat grains, a British school-dinner staple.

clue.text: Long to start late and make a living

indicators.note: starting late means the opening letter of the word is missing

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to begin work later and still pay the bills.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to be paid for work, making a living.

clue.text: Lost virtue accepting student stream

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the student goes inside
lost means astray or gone wrong, so the letters of the word are set in disarray

parts.note: L, for learner, is the usual crossword letter for a student

explanation.surface: A fallen student is taken in by a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' rearranges VIRTUE to RIVUET and 'accepting' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivulet is a very small stream or brook.

clue.text: Watch the pet eat Edward's pudding!

indicators.note: eat means take in, so the name goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: to spot is to see or watch
a dog is a typical pet
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the pet as it devours Edward's dessert!
explanation.walkthrough: 'eat' signals the container. Spotted dog is a British steamed suet pudding studded with currants, a cousin of spotted dick.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted dog is a suet dessert studded with dried fruit.

clue.text: Fed up with one worker being insubordinate

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Fed up with a colleague who refuses to obey orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF; 'Fed up' reads as one phrase meaning annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiant means openly resisting authority, as a rebellious subordinate does.

clue.text: Insurance gets media publicity

explanation.surface: An insurance company attracts attention in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover in an insurance policy is protection against loss; press and broadcast reporting of an event is its news exposure.

clue.text: Show assessment to the audience

indicators.note: to the audience means as heard by listeners, so the word is spelt by its sound

parts.note: a review is a critical assessment

explanation.surface: A performance is critically judged in front of its spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a stage show of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: Tender belonging to French royal

parts.note: of expresses belonging, as in the house of the king
French gives F
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the queen

explanation.surface: Something gentle that belongs to a French king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective, gentle, but is the noun or verb sense of a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a formal bid, which is a proposal to supply at a stated price.

clue.text: Better turn up on time for agreement

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece above the second
in a down clue turn up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A gambler arrives punctually to make a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as a gambler, but is the verb, to outdo; 'turn up' reverses CAP to PAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement or treaty between parties.

clue.text: Missing leader in seven-nil thrashing for 27

indicators.note: thrashing means beating about, so the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
missing leader means the first letter of the following word is dropped

explanation.surface: A team without its captain still wins a seven-nil rout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing leader' drops the S from seven-nil, leaving EVENNIL, which 'thrashing' rearranges. 27 is ANIMATE, in the sense of bring to life.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven something is to give it life and energy, the verb sense of 27.

clue.text: Pass on inspiration to make a cartoon

explanation.surface: An artist inspires others to produce an animated film.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to breathe life or spirit into someone, and also to produce moving pictures from drawings.

clue.text: A cobbler's favourite dance?

parts.note: a shoemaker shapes shoes on a foot-shaped block called a last, so his ideal dance would be a ballroom one named after that tool

explanation.definitionFit: The closing waltz of an evening dance, punning on the cobbler's last, his foot-shaped form.
